analysis.investment_thesis: Affle is a genuinely impressive mobile programmatic advertising platform with a 7-year revenue CAGR of 45%, zero meaningful debt, and consistently positive free cash flow — rare attributes in ad-tech. The problem is that recent earnings growth has decelerated to ~22-29% (2024-2025) while the P/E stays at 47.2, pushing the PEG to ~2.1, which is above the level where I'd add aggressively.
key_strengths: Debt/Equity of 0.01 and INR 1,047 Cr cash on balance sheet — this is a capital-light, self-funding compounder with no existential balance sheet risk
FCF positive every single year (2020–2025), growing from INR 41 Cr to INR 266 Cr — real cash earnings backing the P&L

Multi-platform portfolio (Appnext, Mediasmart, Jampp, RevX, YouAppi) creates a programmatic stack spanning discovery, retargeting, and omnichannel — hard to displace once embedded in a client's marketing stack
key_risks: Growth deceleration is visible: revenue grew 28% in FY25 vs 45% 7-year CAGR; net profit grew 29% in FY25 — the high-growth phase may be maturing
P/E 47.2 with PEG ~2.1 on recent growth means the stock needs to consistently re-accelerate earnings to justify the multiple — a tough bar to clear each quarter
Operating margin of 18.1% is thin for what should be a high-IP digital platform; acquisition-heavy strategy inflates goodwill and adds integration risk
red_flags: Historical 45% revenue CAGR is unlikely to continue at scale — the law of large numbers means FY26 growth must slow further
Investing CF of -INR 572 Cr in 2024 and recurring large outflows suggest growth is partly acquisition-driven, which carries integration and goodwill risk
analysis.detailed_analysis: Affle operates at the intersection of two things I like: a growing market (mobile internet advertising in India and emerging Asia) and a business model with real network effects (more consumer data → better CPCU targeting → more advertiser spend → more publisher relationships). The company has compounded at 45% for seven years by riding India's smartphone and app economy, and the platform breadth gives it cross-sell levers its smaller competitors lack. OCF was INR 426 Cr in 2025 and FCF was INR 266 Cr — this is a cash machine.
